extracted.intended_audience: participants, contractors, administrators, and legal counsel involved in FCC programs (USF, Lifeline, ACP, TRS, NDBEDP) and Suspension and Debarment Officials
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Communications Commission implementing rules governing exclusions (suspensions/debarments), exceptions, covered transactions, disclosure obligations, transition/continuation policies, and review procedures for participants and agency officials across FCC programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission delegation of exception authority to SDO
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delegates exclusive authority to its SDO in the first instance, as the Commission's sole designee, to grant exceptions to exclusions. Neither the Commission, nor the Chairperson of the Commission, will rule on exceptions in the first instance, but the Commission may consider applications for review of an SDO decision on exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exception, if granted, permits an excluded person to participate in one or more particular covered transactions as specified by the SDO; the exception must be in writing and state the reasons for deviating from Executive Order 12549. A person may petition for an exception during SDO proceedings or as provided in related sections; exceptions for one agency do not extend to other agencies' covered transactions. Any exceptions granted by the SDO shall be subject to conditions (see conditions entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating exception requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating requests for exceptions, the SDO shall evaluate the particular services provided by the excluded person and the availability of alternate providers in the areas served, the typical terms of any contracts that may exist between the provider and its beneficiaries, any federal or state certification requirements that may be applicable, when the misconduct resulting in the exclusion occurred, and in the case of exclusions by other agencies, when the exclusion was issued and how much longer the exclusion will remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because exceptions are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, the SDO has discretion to consider any other factors that may be relevant, and shall balance providing continued services to beneficiaries and protecting program integrity. The SDO shall consult with the bureaus or offices responsible for the program and the Office of General Counsel. The proponent of an exception bears the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, any facts asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions attachable to exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any exceptions granted by the SDO may be subject to appropriate conditions such as mandatory audits, additional reporting requirements, compliance agreements (with approval of the Office of General Counsel), monitoring, or any other forms of effective oversight supplemental to that already provided under FCC programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions are imposed as the SDO considers appropriate to ensure excluded persons for whom exceptions are granted comply with Commission program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exceptions for Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations/enrollment representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: No exceptions shall be permitted for Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations or for enrollment representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such entities/persons are categorically precluded from obtaining exceptions under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of initial suspension vs final suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial suspension decision shall prevent the suspended party from enrolling new customers or otherwise entering into new covered transactions, but an initial suspension made before a party has had the opportunity to oppose shall not trigger discontinuations of service or require beneficiaries/program administrators to find alternative service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any discontinuations or substitution of provider requirements are not effective until after the suspension process results in a final suspension decision or the time to contest the initial suspension has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO/Commission review timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO must make a written decision addressing any petition for reconsideration within 45 days of receiving the petition (may extend for good cause). The Commission will attempt in good faith to issue a written decision addressing any application for review of a final suspension or debarment decision within 180 days of receiving the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are target timeframes for administrative review of exclusion-related decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempted Commission transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transactions involving the Commission that are not related to or do not arise in connection with the Covered Programs shall be exempted transactions under this part. An application to the Commission to participate in a competitive process (short-form application) is also an exempted transaction, but a subsequent long-form application based on competitive results is not exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form stage reviews are limited accordingly; long-form winners must satisfy covered-transaction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded persons prohibited from advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person that is suspended or debarred may not, during their period of exclusion, serve on a Commission advisory committee or comparable Commission group or task force established by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an already-appointed advisory member is suspended or debarred, they shall be removed. 'Suspended or debarred' includes persons suspended/debarred by the Commission or listed on SAM.gov Exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Commission covered transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining covered transactions under §180.200, covered transactions include any transaction at the primary tier between a person and the Commission or any agents of the Commission (including USF, TRS, NDBEDP Administrators). Hiring of enrollment representatives by marketing organizations is considered a covered transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions between two primary tier participants (other than the Commission) are considered lower tier transactions per §6001.210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of tier participants by program
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and lower tier participants are defined by program: e.g., for E-Rate/Cybersecurity/Rural Health Care, primary tier includes schools/libraries/health care providers and service providers they select; for High-Cost/Lifeline/TRS/ACP, primary tier are service providers requesting/receiving support; NDBEDP primary tier are certified programs requesting reimbursements; lower tier includes persons engaged in covered transactions (including enrollment representatives employed by marketing organizations). Beneficiaries are not primary or lower tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These program-specific definitions determine which transactions are subject to the part's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower-tier covered transactions criteria (material role/principal/$25,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower-tier transactions for various programs include contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, or agents where (1) such person has a material role relating to or significantly affecting claims for disbursements related to the program; (2) such person is considered a 'principal'; or (3) the amount of the transaction is expected to be at least $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is repeated across program-specific subsections (High-Cost, E-Rate, RHC, TRS, NDBEDP, ACP Outreach Grant Program) to determine lower-tier coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifeline and ACP special coverage rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Lifeline and ACP programs, supported transactions involving any participant (except the primary tier carrier or service provider) are covered regardless of tier or dollar value, including those reimbursed based on number of subscribers enrolled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, Lifeline/ACP transactions involving contractors/persons are covered if they have a material role, are principals, or exceed $25,000 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to verify before entering covered transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are responsible for determining whether they are entering into a covered transaction with an appropriate person based on its disclosures. You must verify that the person is not excluded or disqualified by checking SAM.gov Exclusions, collecting certifications, or adding a clause/condition to the contract. These requirements apply whether entering transactions at the next lower tier or same tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If verifying via SAM.gov, you must also check the FCC's list of previously suspended or debarred entities. For employment contracts, the FCC does not require checking SAM.gov before making salary payments pursuant to that contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and transition obligations upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are in covered transactions with an excluded person, you must transition to an alternate provider or discontinue using that excluded principal within the period required by the SDO, except in rare cases where the SDO permits continuation for a limited period. You may not renew or extend covered transactions (other than no-cost time extensions) with any excluded person unless an exception is provided by the SDO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO will evaluate services provided, contract terms, certification requirements, and availability of alternates; ensure transition periods allow for competitive bidding or provider certification when needed. The SDO may permit limited continuation subject to compliance measures (e.g., audits, monitoring) if in public interest and protective of consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO must provide smooth and expedited transition and require continued service during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion orders shall provide a smooth and expedited transition to alternative providers to the maximum extent possible. The SDO shall require that during any transitional period, the excluded providers continue providing services to their beneficiaries consistent with Commission rules and with their contractual obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alternates cannot be identified quickly, the SDO may allow limited extension but should strongly consider administrative remedies (compliance agreements, audits, reporting, monitoring). Compliance agreements require OGC approval and consultation with administering bureau or office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices to affected beneficiaries during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: After determining the transition period, the SDO shall require excluded providers to provide timely notices to affected customers. Notices shall include: (i) a statement that the participating provider has been suspended or debarred and the date it will be ceasing operations; (ii) a statement that users should obtain service from another provider; (iii) a listing of names and contact information for other authorized providers in the jurisdiction; and (iv) a statement that the excluded provider will continue to provide service until it must cease operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining notice requirements, the SDO should consider program-specific notice provisions (especially for Lifeline). If continuation is permitted, beneficiaries shall be advised and may opt to continue with that provider by notifying the SDO within 30 days after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate cessation for marketing organizations, enrollment representatives, consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO shall require that marketing organizations, enrollment representatives, or consultants who have been suspended or debarred shall immediately cease their operations related to covered transactions. No exceptions or transitional periods shall be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participants shall not have the option to continue doing business with such entities or persons during the period of their suspension or debarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing requirements to downstream participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Before entering into a covered transaction with another participant at the same or lower tier, you must require that participant to comply with part 180, subpart C of this title, as supplemented by this part, as a condition of participation, by collecting a certification or including a term or condition to this effect in your transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must also require that participant to pass that same requirement to each person with whom it enters into a covered transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure obligations for lower and primary tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Before entering into a covered transaction, all lower tier participants shall be obligated to notify and disclose to any other participants (regardless of tier) the information described in §180.335. Disclosures shall be made under penalty of perjury. If no disclosures are required, participant must certify under penalty of perjury that none are required. If participating in competitive bidding, the information must be disclosed at bid submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided, disclosures must be simultaneously submitted to the USF Administrator, ACP Administrator, TRS Fund Administrator, NDBEDP Administrator, and the FCC. Failures to disclose permit the participant with whom the lower tier participant is doing business to terminate the transaction or pursue other remedies. Participants must also comply with §180.350 notifications upon learning new information, providing such notifications to administrators and the higher/lower tier participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual disclosure statements for Lifeline participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and lower tier participants in the Lifeline program shall file annual disclosure statements, upon penalty of perjury, reporting all required disclosures or certifying that they have no reportable disclosures to make. Primary tier participants may also file on behalf of lower tier participants with whom they have a direct relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation that substantiates required certifications shall be provided to the Commission upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment representative disclosure limited to marketing organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment representatives of Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations shall be required to disclose only to the marketing organizations with whom they are employed or seek employment the information described in §180.355 (pertaining to exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing organizations are required to obtain these disclosures for review by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACP Outreach Grant Program streamlined disclosure filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and lower tier participants in the ACP Outreach Grant Program shall file annual disclosure statements, but lower tier participants need only file their expanded disclosures with the primary tier participant for whom they perform work (or with the lower tier participants for whom they perform work in contracts among lower tier participants). Primary tier participants shall then file on behalf of all lower tier participants with which they have a relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This streamlines administration; documentation substantiating certifications must still be provided to the Commission upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: USF competitive bidding disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For USF competitive bidding, the Commission's review at the short-form stage shall be limited to the status of the applicant (i.e., whether the applicant is presently excluded or disqualified), while a winning bidder will be required to make the additional required disclosures upon submission of a long-form application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form stage does not substitute for later long-form disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific channels and addresses for disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures required by §§180.335–180.350 shall be made not only to the Commission but also to the USF Administrator, TRS Fund Administrator, NDBEDP Administrator, and ACP Administrator. Specific email addresses and mailing addresses are provided for submitting disclosures (e.g., USFDisclosures@fcc.gov, USFDisclosures@usac.org, TRSreports@fcc.gov, NDBEDPreports@fcc.gov, plus mailing addresses to specified FCC bureaus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed submission channels appropriate to program and disclosure type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may expand disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosures required under this section shall also include such disclosures as the Commission may require, in implementing these suspension and debarment rules, under any updated information collections or other disclosure obligations that may be required for Lifeline, TRS and NDBEDP programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must comply with any updated disclosure obligations adopted by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting terminations and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: For terminations of public transactions: (1) A termination 'for cause or default' shall not include the denial of funding requests for minor technical or procedural errors (as determined by the SDO); but a termination of a previously approved funding request because of serious errors or misconduct by a participant requires disclosure; and (2) Otherwise reportable terminations that may be pending appeal must be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish minor procedural denials from serious misconduct that triggers disclosure obligations; disclose pending appeals where terminations are otherwise reportable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of unfavorable disclosures and available remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfavorable disclosures by primary or lower tier participants shall be evaluated on a case-by-case basis and will not automatically trigger exclusion or denial. Unfavorable disclosures should be outcome-determinative only where factual circumstances require denial of a transaction or possibly an exclusion (or an LDP) to protect program integrity. Bureaus/offices and Administrators may consider number of providers available and other transition/continuation factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated bureau/office authority may determine remedies appropriate in light of disclosures, including: approving transactions contingent on administrative agreements (e.g., compliance plans), additional monitoring/oversight, denying applications, terminating ongoing transactions, or referring to an SDO to consider a limited denial of participation. Any compliance agreement requires Office of General Counsel approval. Administrators must develop policies/procedures governing review of disclosures consistent with §180.340 and obtain prior approval from relevant bureau or office before taking actions outside those policies.
